content:
Apple TV has long been hailed as the "new HBO" because they prioritize quality over quantity. But recently, this streaming platform has begun actively expanding its lineup to the point where I can't keep up.

Apple TV is simultaneously boosting both quality and quantity, entering a new phase as a streaming platform

Since Apple TV first launched in 2019, I've maintained my subscription, and historically the platform usually only had one or two shows I'd actually want to watch.

This model resembles HBO, which has always built its brand on fewer but stronger titles, with overall quality generally higher than its competitors.

However, over the past few years, Apple's output has steadily grown, while the hit rate has also noticeably improved.

The result is: Apple now has so many great shows that I simply can't keep up.

Below are the Apple TV shows currently airing new episodes each week:

  • Ted Lasso, one of my all-time favorite shows
  • Slow Horses, another of the best series in Apple history
  • Dark Matter, a sci-fi series whose first season had me hooked, but I haven't started season two yet
  • Brothers, a brand-new half-hour comedy starring Will Arnett and Woody Harrelson that looks pretty entertaining
  • Last Seen, a brand-new thriller I've heard great things about but haven't watched
  • Then there's Women in Blue and Knife Edge — these two I might watch if I happen to have free time, but they don't make the priority list right now

I'm really looking forward to catching up on Dark Matter; season one was already one of my favorite sci-fi shows, right behind Severance and Pluribus. But I just can't find the time to start season two. I also enjoy binge-watching lighthearted half-hour comedies, so Brothers is already queued up.

I'm into crime thrillers and shows involving families, so Last Seen is right up my alley. Even though Stephen King has recommended it, I still haven't gotten around to watching it.

The above are only the shows currently airing.

I haven't finished Silo season three yet, and I haven't even started Sugar season two — despite the good reviews and my own love of the show. If I dropped my other streaming platforms, theoretically I could binge more on Apple, but there are great shows on other services pulling me away too.

October is just around the corner, and Apple has as many as seven brand-new series and films premiering — the most I can recall in a single month.

All in all, I'm genuinely delighted at how well Apple TV is doing now. The fact that Apple won more Emmys than HBO this year is absolutely justified.

What do you think of Apple TV's current and recent slate of shows? Feel free to share your thoughts in the comments section.

Apple TV costs US$14.99 per month, or you can get a discount through the Apple One bundle.
